newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reports clears Kingstream - An Feng merger.
newsitem.headline: Reports clears Kingstream - An Feng merger.

text.p: Perth-based Kingstream Resources NL said on Monday an independent expert's report on the proposed merger with Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd had found the proposal fair and reasonable.
Kingstream said the proposed merger is to be effected by Kingstream acquiring up to 100 percent of An Feng in exchange for 615 million new fully paid Kingstream shares issued at A$1.30 each.
Kingstream would also issue 6.3 million new five year options exercisable at A$1.10 a share.

As part of the merger deal, Kingstream shareholders would be granted free five year options to subscribe for Kingstream shares in the ratio of one new option exerrcisable at A$1.10 for every 2.25 Kingstream shares held.
After the merger, Kingstream shareholders would own 19.7 percent of the merged group.
An Feng is Taiwan's second largest steel producer, taking a 31 percent market share since it began production in 1991, Kingstream said.

The report, prepared by Grant Samuel and Associates Pty Ltd, found that the strategic logic of the merger was compelling and the merger proposal enhanced the prospects of the AFK steel project, also called the Mid West Iron and Steel Project, in Western Australia being developed.
The report anticipated Kingstream's share price would be higher after the acquisition of An Feng, Kingstream said.

This would reflect the transformation of Kingstream into a vertically integrated steel producer with access to an earnings stream, reduced risk profile and enhanced prospects for realising value from the AFK steel project, Kingstream said.
The net asset backing per share of the merged company would increase to A$1.20 from 62 cents on a fully diluted basis at December 31, 1996, as a result of the merger, it said.
This excluded the value of the AFK steel project, which would increase the net asset backing, Kingstream said.
An Feng and Kingstream plan to build a A$1.4 billion steelmaking project in Western Australia, with construction to begin in the third quarter of 1997.
Kingstream shares were two cents firmer at 94 cents at 11.25 a.m. (0125 GMT).
